solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fancy pastries? That is where to buy them

indicators.note: as a verb-like adjective, fancy suggests something elaborated or reworked, so the letters of pastries are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders about fancy pastries and is told where they can be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy pastries' looks like the thing defined, but 'Fancy' is the anagram signal and the definition is the shop at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pâtisserie is a French-style cake shop, the place where such pastries are sold.

clue.text: Smart borders provided calm

indicators.note: borders means lies on both sides of, so the word for smart surrounds the next piece

parts.note: smart can mean brisk or quick, which is pacy
provided means if, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: Neat edges made something look tranquil, as in a tidy garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or quieten someone, making them calm.

clue.text: Fibrous tissue had stuck in part of joint

indicators.note: stuck in means pushed inside, so the letter for had goes into the joint piece

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a mortise and tenon joint in woodwork
had is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Tough tissue had got lodged in a body joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests the body, matching the tissue, but it is a carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a cord of tough fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Soft drink all pass round R&A twice keeps one up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole string reads from bottom to top
keeps means holds inside, so the letter for one goes in

parts.note: taken as written
the R&A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews; twice means its letters are used two times

indicators.note: round means going around, so the words all pass are placed around the golf letters

parts.note: taken as written
the second use of the golf club's letters, this time inside the word pass
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A soft drink is passed round a golf club twice, and keeps one person going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'R&A twice' means the golf club's two letters are placed at two separate points, not side by side; 'keeps' then adds the one, and 'up' turns the whole string, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsaparilla is a sweet fizzy drink flavoured with the root of a tropical vine.

clue.text: Where Bonaparte planned battle with no heart for it?

definitions.text: Where Bonaparte planned battle with no heart for it?

indicators.note: planned means worked out or arranged, so the remaining letters are arranged afresh
the heart of a word is its middle, so the central pair of letters goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where Napoleon plotted a fight he had no stomach for.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous palindrome 'Able was I ere I saw Elba' lurks behind it: BATTLE without its middle TT is BALE, rearranged to give the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island in 1814 and planned his return, leading to Waterloo.

clue.text: Bully — one meat I'd tin when pickled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: pickled means preserved but also drunk and muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving two letters

explanation.surface: A cook threatens to can some preserved meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' looks like bully beef, tinned corned beef, which suits the meat and tin, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate is to frighten someone into doing something, which is what a bully does.

clue.text: Show no respect for grass

definitions.meaning: slang verb meaning to disrespect or insult someone
a tall Mediterranean grass used for cordage and basketwork

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop disrespecting an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' tempts as British slang for an informer, but here it is the plant: diss is a coarse reed-like grass of North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary words: the slang verb for insulting, and the name of a cord grass.

clue.text: Daydreams as Gemini being versatile does

indicators.note: versatile means adaptable and changeable, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: An astrology note says that Geminis, being adaptable, are given to fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to picture things in the mind, which is what a dreamer does; both verbs are in the third person.

clue.text: Busy cross roads around New York providing material for cameos

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the next piece
busy suggests bustling about, so the letters are set moving

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A busy road junction near New York is where materials for small films are found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy cross roads' looks like a crossroads, but 'Busy' is the anagram signal working on the cross letter and the roads together; 'cameos' are carved brooches, not film appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a banded onyx whose coloured layers are carved for cameo brooches.

clue.text: Submit for publication short story about Eve's origin, leaving nothing out

indicators.note: about here means around, so the story goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a conte is a short story, especially as a French literary genre
in Genesis Eve was made from Adam's rib

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so the word out goes without the letter for nothing

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shown by the letter O

explanation.surface: A writer offers a magazine a short story about where Eve came from, complete and uncut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving nothing out' reads as 'omitting nothing', but it means the word out leaving its O; 'short story' is the French literary term conte.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute is to send a piece of writing to a newspaper or magazine for printing.

clue.text: Is it just the taxman that's after soccer bosses?

indicators.note: after puts the taxman's letters following the soccer bosses' letters

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English soccer
IR is the Inland Revenue, the old British tax authority

explanation.surface: A rueful question whether it is fair that the tax authorities are pursuing football's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and just are synonyms, both meaning treating people rightly and evenly.

clue.text: Wings of Scottish Kirk lessen after Disruption role of senior elder

indicators.note: the 1843 split of the Church of Scotland; as a disruption it breaks up the letters
wings are the two edges, so only the outer three letters at each end of the phrase are kept

explanation.surface: The flanks of the Church of Scotland shrank after the great 1843 schism.
explanation.walkthrough: The Disruption of 1843 was when the Free Church broke away from the Church of Scotland. Keeping the three end letters of each wing gives SCO and IRK; with LESSEN they make the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish Presbyterian churches the session clerk is the elder who keeps the minutes of the kirk session.

clue.text: This dance of Kate Moss is for all dancing

definitions.note: a whole-noun description standing for the first word of a song title; the answer is used as the name of the piece

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supermodel's dance routine is offered to everyone to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Moss is not the model: Katie Moss composed the 1911 song 'The Floral Dance', about Helston's spring festival in Cornwall. The definition stands for the missing first word of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Katie Moss's best-known song is titled The Floral Dance, so the word naming her dance is its first title word.

clue.text: One of 7, favourite one for a skin condition

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the new letters replace the letter a

parts.note: the answer to 7-down is the plural of imago, so one of them is an imago, an adult insect
a teacher's pet is a favourite
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cross-reference picks one of 7-down and pairs it with a favourite to name a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: Solvers need 7-down first: IMAGINES is the plural of IMAGO, the final adult stage of an insect. Replace its A with PET and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection of the skin, producing crusty sores.

clue.text: Jargon for Vergeltungswaffe: nuclear modification on a rocket head

parts.note: German for retaliation weapon, the V of the wartime V-1 and V-2 rockets

indicators.note: a modification is an alteration, so the letters of nuclear are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A German term for a reprisal weapon, given a nuclear upgrade and mounted on a missile warhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime V-1 and V-2 flying bombs were named Vergeltungswaffen; the clue takes their V, then an anagram of NUCLEAR, A, and R from the top of 'rocket'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernacular means the everyday language or dialect of a group, close to its own special jargon.

clue.text: Introduce her to eBay's hard wheeling and dealing in buttons and bows

indicators.note: wheeling means turning round and round, so the letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: here the s of the possessive is a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to get a woman into tough eBay trading in buttons and bows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeling and dealing' looks like one stock phrase, but 'wheeling' is the anagram signal and 'dealing' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Haberdashery is the trade in sewing goods and small dress accessories such as ribbons, buttons and thread.

clue.text: Change I made in a carbon copy for reader perhaps

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: cc is the abbreviation for carbon copy, as on an email

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of I made are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes an edit they made to a duplicate document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reader' is not someone reading: in British universities a reader is a senior lecturer just below professor, so an example of an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A university reader is a senior scholar, one kind of academic, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Sign name young member of family adopts for rising star group

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the family member holds the next piece

parts.note: a scion is a descendant or heir of a family

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A young relative takes on a star sign as a name, aiming for a career on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger suspects a slip: 'Sign name' seems to add nothing to the wordplay, which is SCION holding ORP (PRO turned upwards by 'rising').
explanation.definitionFit: The Scorpion is the constellation Scorpius, a group of stars in the southern sky.

clue.text: Clubs can have people in stitches almost laughing out loud

indicators.note: in places the stitches piece within the pair of other pieces

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
a nation is a people

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side, so stitches suggest aching

explanation.surface: A comedy club has the audience in stitches, nearly roaring with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger notes that 'in' sits a little awkwardly as the insertion signal, since the stitches piece goes inside the clubs-and-people pair rather than the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachinnation is a formal word for loud, convulsive laughter.

clue.text: In USA nuts Ohio tops Rhode Island as butternut source

indicators.note: in puts the Ohio letter inside the scrambled letters
nuts means crazy, so the letters of USA are jumbled

parts.note: O is the old abbreviation for Ohio
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: American nuts from Ohio top those from Rhode Island as a source of butternuts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'tops' means comes above, so the SOUA part sits over RI.
explanation.definitionFit: The souari is a tall South American tree whose large edible nuts are called butternuts.

clue.text: Current money rate's adjusted upward

indicators.note: in a down clue upward means the letters read from the bottom up
adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s here counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: The current interest rate on money has been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective about the rate, but it is a noun: a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flow of water or air, a current.

clue.text: Elder baffled by computer technology that's dilapidated

indicators.note: baffled means confused, so the letters of the word elder are mixed up

parts.note: ICT stands for information and communications technology, the British school subject

explanation.surface: An older person is bewildered by computers and feels decrepit.
explanation.definitionFit: Derelict describes a building or vehicle left to fall into ruin, in a dilapidated state.

clue.text: Tailored coats will incorporate conservative buttonhole

indicators.note: incorporate means take into the body, so the reworked coats hold the next letter
tailored means cut and reshaped, so the letters of coats are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor's made-to-measure coats will include a buttonhole of traditional design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttonhole' fits the tailoring picture as a slit for a button, but here it is a verb: to stop and talk to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to detain them for a talk, just as to accost is to approach and address.

clue.text: Main point of G&T is being tipsy

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady with drink, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: G&T is gin and tonic, giving the letters G and T

explanation.surface: Someone claims the whole point of a gin and tonic is getting a little drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of something is its essence or central idea.

clue.text: The postal system in Motherwell is first-class

indicators.note: in places the first-class letters inside the Motherwell letters

parts.note: ML is the postcode area code for Motherwell, a town in Scotland
A1 means first-class, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: A claim that the postal service in a Scottish town is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: Motherwell's postcode area is ML, which fits the postal theme of the surface; A1 for 'first-class' becomes AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is the system for carrying letters and parcels, as in the Royal Mail.

clue.text: One a little confused about English writing (or reading) maybe

definitions.text: One a little confused about English writing (or reading) maybe

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters go around the English and writing pieces
confused means jumbled, so the letters of a little are mixed

parts.note: R stands for one of the three Rs, reading, 'riting and 'rithmetic

explanation.surface: A person who is somewhat muddled about written English, and perhaps reading too.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of someone unable to read or write; the blogger notes that strictly R stands for reading rather than writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An illiterate person cannot read or write, so is lost with written language.

clue.text: Queeg's command omits one punishment

indicators.note: omits means leaves out, so the ship's name loses the letter for one

parts.note: Captain Queeg commands the USS Caine in the novel The Caine Mutiny
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A captain's order skips one disciplinary measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'command' looks like an order Queeg gives, but it is the ship he commands, the Caine, in Herman Wouk's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane was a rod used for corporal punishment, especially in schools.

clue.text: Revolutionary views stir most up round Bourbon state

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the state's letters
up here means in upheaval or stirred up, so the letters of stir most are rearranged

parts.note: KY is the abbreviation for Kentucky, home of bourbon whiskey

explanation.surface: Political ideas agitate people around a state famous for whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bourbon' suggests the French royal house, a fitting partner for revolution, but it is the whiskey of Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotskyism is the doctrine of permanent world revolution associated with Leon Trotsky.
